newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Thomson BankWatch upgrades Malaysia's rating to A+.
newsitem.headline: Thomson BankWatch upgrades Malaysia's rating to A+.

text.p: The U.S. rating firm Thomson BankWatch announced it has upgraded Malaysia's sovereign risk rating to A+ from A.
It said in a statement that Malaysia had overcome overheating fears and was headed "towards a reassuring soft landing".

"Fears of loan growth and a sharp leap in the current account deficit during last year's first half have subsided considerably, and the country's economic fundamentals have proven to be as steady as ever," BankWatch said.
Though growth in manufacturing, construction and agriculture were forecast to ease slightly in 1997, this did not indicate an economic slowdown.

"Instead, Malaysia is beginning to show signs of approaching a steadier and more sustainable pace of economic expansion," the statement quoted Betty J. Starkey, BankWatch's director of sovereign risk, as saying.
In addition, Malaysia's "prudent fiscal and monetary management and stable political environment" should further reduce current account imbalances and help improve competitiveness, he said.
"For these reasons, we have upgraded Malaysia's sovereign risk rating to A+," Starkey said.
